title: Get Hard
about: A millionaire facing prison hires the man who washes his car to toughen him up before he goes inside.
cue: Serve the mains when Darnell starts the training.
faces: James King's Bel Air steak frites
I never did time, but I can cook. Thirty days of prison food starts tonight, James, so eat your plain rice.

Darnell's Car WashGet HardPrison training starts at dinner.Every recipe serves 4.
    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersCar wash corner store wingsCrisp baked wings in hot sauce butter, ranch for dippingHow to make it1.2kg chicken wings2 tsp baking powder100ml hot sauce50g butter150ml ranch dressingBake the chicken wings tossed with the baking powder and salt at 220°C for 45 minutes.Toss in the hot sauce melted with the butter and serve with the ranch.Bel Air salmon roe blinisWarm blinis with chive crème fraîche and salmon roeHow to make it16 small blinis150g crème fraîche1 bunch chives1 lemon150g smoked salmon50g salmon roe1 bunch dillWarm the small blinis at 180°C for 4 minutes.Mix the crème fraîche with the chopped chives and lemon zest.Top each blini with a spoon of the cream, a ribbon of smoked salmon and half a teaspoon of salmon roe.Finish with a tiny dill sprig and a squeeze of lemon and arrange on a platter.MainsDarnell's family barbecue chickenBarbecue glazed chicken thighs with mac and cheese and silverbeetHow to make it1kg chicken thighs200ml barbecue sauce300g macaroni30g butter2 tbsp plain flour500ml full cream milk200g cheddar1 bunch silverbeetBake the chicken thighs at 200°C for 25 minutes, brush with the barbecue sauce and bake some more.Make mac and cheese from the macaroni, the butter, the flour, the milk and the cheddar.Serve with the sautéed silverbeet.James King's Bel Air steak fritesThe last fancy dinner King thinks he's getting before San QuentinHow to make it4 sirloin steaks1kg potatoes, cut into chips3 tbsp olive oil60g butter, softened2 garlic cloves, crushed1 bunch flat-leaf parsley100g rocket1 lemonsalt and pepper, to tasteHeat the oven to 220°C. Toss the chips in 2 tbsp oil and salt and bake, turning once, until crisp.Mash the butter with the garlic and chopped parsley.Sear the steaks in a very hot pan to your liking, then rest with a slice of herb butter on each.Dress the rocket with lemon and the last of the oil and serve with the steak and chips.SweetsSan Quentin chocolate pudding cupsStovetop chocolate pudding chilled in cupsHow to make it600ml milk80g caster sugar30g cocoa powder3 tbsp cornflour100g dark chocolatevanilla extract, to taste150ml thickened cream60g chocolate biscuitssea salt flakes, to tasteWhisk the milk, the caster sugar, the cocoa, the cornflour and a pinch of salt in a saucepan over medium heat until it thickens, about 6 minutes.Off the heat, stir in the chopped dark chocolate and the vanilla until smooth.Pour into the serving dishes, cover the surface and chill 2 hours.Top with whipped cream, crushed chocolate biscuits with a pinch of flaky salt and chocolate curls.DrinksKing's cucumber jalapeño margaritaTequila, cucumber, lime and jalapeño with a salted rimHow to make it1 continental cucumber1 jalapeño180ml tequila5 limes60ml agave syrupsalt flakes, to taste2 cups ice50ml waterBlitz the continental cucumber with the water and strain.Rim the glasses with lime and salt.For each drink, muddle the slices of jalapeño in a shaker, add the tequila, the cucumber juice, the lime juice and the agave, shake with ice and strain over fresh ice.Garnish with a cucumber ribbon.For non-drinkers, top the cucumber, lime and agave with soda instead.Vintage champagne by the glassJames King's mansion pour, before the sentence.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
